dispositions.rationale: The slice changes the enforces lists in four front-matter blocks and adds tests. It changes no code path that writes, so it creates no in-scope obligation about what a check leaves behind. The sentence the objection read as a guarantee was the what-if answer's reason the question does not apply; the amended text says that in those words and answers the repeat question with ARO-A17.

parts.statement: Every rule in the standard appears in exactly one `enforces` list.
The rules are assigned to the specific lenses listed in ARO-D1.
A missing owner or duplicate owner is rejected and the failure names the rule.

obligations.source: “Every rule of the acceptance-criteria standard gets exactly one owning lens” and the ARO-D1 ownership table.
obligations.statement: Every standard rule has exactly one owner, using the ownership assignment in ARO-D1.

parts.statement: Each emitted prompt equals its lens body plus the four shared contracts.
Each emitted prompt contains exactly the rules declared by that lens.
Each emitted prompt contains the exact ARO-D1 rule assignment, and a mismatch names the lens.

obligations.source: “The emitter puts exactly those rules into the lens's prompt” and “The emitter suite ... pin[s] ... how a prompt is composed.”
obligations.statement: The emitter constructs each lens prompt from the required body, contracts and owned rules.

parts.statement: A lens naming a rule absent from the standard is refused as `no-lenses` without writing output.
An objection missing its target, ground rule or a scenario part is refused as `schema`.
An objection with a field outside its schema is refused as `schema`.
Missing or schema-invalid obligation-reduction workings are refused as `invalid-workings`.
An undischarged obligation part without a corresponding objection is refused as `unreported-residue`.
A ground outside the reporting lens's ownership is refused as `ground-outside-lens`.

obligations.source: ARO-D1 says the record check accepts an objection only under its lens's rules; ARO-D2 says the suites pin what the record check refuses.
obligations.statement: The emitter and record checker refuse the malformed configurations and reports assigned to this slice.

parts.statement: The lens registry contains exactly behavioural-outcome, obligation-reduction, set-consistency and what-if.
The attack actually runs exactly those four lenses.

obligations.source: “A lens is one of the four reviewers the criteria attack runs” and ARO-D2 says the suites pin “which lenses run.”
obligations.statement: The criteria attack uses exactly the four named lenses.

parts.statement: The six existing prompt, unknown-rule and record-refusal checks continue to pass.
The suite gains checks for the five previously untested requirements.

obligations.source: ARO-D2 says six existing tests “must still pass” and “The slice adds a test for each of the other five where none exists.”
obligations.statement: Existing attack-surface behavior remains pinned while ownership changes, and missing tests are added.

parts.statement: The checker schema behavior serves ACQ-A20.
The exact lens set serves ACQ-A22.
Prompt composition serves the assigned portion of ACQ-A23.
Complete ownership and emitted assignment serve the assigned portion of ACQ-A24.
Prompt rule propagation and unknown-rule refusal serve ACQ-A26.
Workings and residue validation serve ACQ-A28.
Ground ownership validation serves ACQ-A29.

obligations.source: “This spec serves seven parent criteria” together with the Traceability table.
obligations.statement: The child spec serves the stated portions of its seven parent criteria.

parts.statement: An empty registry is refused as `no-lenses`.
An absent standard is refused as `no-standard`.

obligations.source: “An empty registry and an absent standard are the existing `no-lenses` and `no-standard` refusals.”
obligations.statement: Missing foundational inputs produce their established refusal codes.

parts.statement: Running any check does not mutate state.
Repeating a check against unchanged inputs produces the same answer.

obligations.source: “Every check is a read, so running it twice or with nothing changed answers the same way.”
obligations.statement: Every check is read-only and stable when repeated without a change in inputs.

parts.statement: `make content-tests` exits 0 for the completed work.

obligations.source: The Continuations entry requires “make content-tests exits 0.”
obligations.statement: The complete content test gate succeeds for the delivered slice.

ground.reason: ARO-D2 promises to pin "which lenses run," but ARO-A2 checks only that the lens registry contains the four expected names. The emitter suite can accept that artifact without observing whether the attack actually emits or executes every registered lens.

objections.objection: A correct registry can pass while the criteria attack omits one of the four promised reviewers.
objections.obligation: The criteria attack runs behavioural-outcome, obligation-reduction, set-consistency and what-if.

scenario.expect: ARO-A2 passes even though the what-if lens never runs.
scenario.given: The registry contains exactly the four required lens names, but the attack's execution path filters out what-if.
scenario.when: The emitter suite performs ARO-A2's registry-set check.

ground.reason: The scope promises that every rule has a lens that can object under it, and ARO-D1 says the record check accepts objections under the owning lens's rules. ARO-A1 checks ownership lists, ARO-A11 checks emitted prompt content, and ARO-A10 checks only rejection of out-of-lens grounds. No criterion checks that a schema-valid objection grounded in an owned rule is accepted.

objections.objection: All ownership and prompt checks can pass while the record checker rejects every valid objection under a newly assigned rule.
objections.obligation: For every standard rule, its owning lens can produce a schema-valid objection that the record check accepts.

scenario.expect: All named suites pass while behavioural-outcome cannot submit an accepted objection grounded in human-measurement.
scenario.given: The ownership lists and emitted prompts exactly match ARO-D1, and invalid records receive every required refusal, but the checker also rejects valid in-lens objections.
scenario.when: The emitter and checker suites run all checks named by ARO-A1 through ARO-A11.

ground.reason: ARO-A2 observes the lens registry, but no criterion observes which lenses the attack actually executes.

objections.objection: The registry can contain exactly the four required lenses while the attack silently skips one or substitutes another at execution time.

scenario.expect: The attack does not run all four required lenses even though every criterion passes.
scenario.given: The registry contains behavioural-outcome, obligation-reduction, set-consistency and what-if, and all prompt and checker tests pass.
scenario.when: The criteria attack runs and its execution path skips what-if.

ground.reason: ARO-A2 requires a failure for an invalid registry but does not require the empty-registry failure to be `no-lenses`.

objections.objection: An empty registry can produce the wrong refusal while satisfying every stated criterion.

scenario.expect: The emitter refuses with a code other than `no-lenses`.
scenario.when: The emitter suite exercises the empty registry and fails as ARO-A2 requires.

ground.reason: No criterion exercises an absent standard or requires the `no-standard` refusal.

objections.objection: The absent-standard boundary can return the wrong result while all criteria pass.

scenario.expect: The emitter proceeds or refuses with a code other than `no-standard`.
scenario.when: The emitter runs after all stated criterion checks pass.

ground.reason: The criteria check outputs and refusals but never observe whether the checks mutate files or other state.

objections.objection: A check can write state while still returning every required prompt, refusal and diagnostic.

scenario.expect: The check produces the required answer but also changes persistent state.
scenario.given: All suites begin in a state that satisfies their asserted outputs.
scenario.when: A criterion check runs and writes a cache or modifies a source file.

ground.reason: No criterion repeats a check against unchanged state and compares the results.

objections.objection: Checks can return different answers on an unchanged second run while all one-run assertions pass.

scenario.expect: The second run returns a different prompt, refusal or result from the first.
scenario.given: The source tree and inputs remain unchanged after a first successful check.
scenario.when: The same check runs a second time.

ground.reason: The criteria exercise two named suites, but none requires the complete `make content-tests` gate to exit 0.

objections.objection: All ARO-A1 through ARO-A11 checks can pass while the promised completion gate remains red.

scenario.expect: `make content-tests` exits nonzero despite every stated criterion check passing.
scenario.given: The emitter and checker suites satisfy ARO-A1 through ARO-A11, but another content test fails.

ground.reason: The 'at a limit' question: ARO-A1 pins a rule appearing in zero lists and in two different lenses' lists, but a rule listed twice inside a single lens's enforces list appears in exactly one list and has exactly one owner, so no criterion fails on it.

objections.objection: A rule duplicated within one lens's enforces list passes every criterion: ARO-A1 sees one owner, and a set-based read of ARO-A11's 'exactly the rules the table lists' sees no difference from the row, so the emitter may put the same rule into a prompt twice with no test failing.

scenario.expect: the suite fails, naming the duplicated rule or its lens, but no criterion requires this
scenario.given: One lens's enforces list in lenses/*/prompt.md names the same rule ID twice, with every rule still owned by exactly one lens
scenario.when: the emitter suite runs the ARO-A1 and ARO-A11 tests

ground.reason: The 'empty input' question: ARO-A6 refuses an objection 'lacking' a part, which pins absence, but an objection whose target, ground rule, or scenario part is present as an empty string is not lacking anything, so no criterion refuses it.

objections.objection: A vacuous objection passes the record check: all required fields present but empty satisfies ARO-A6 and ARO-A7, letting a content-free objection into the record where it can discharge nothing yet still count.

scenario.expect: refusal as 'schema', but ARO-A6 as written covers only missing parts, not empty ones
scenario.given: A report whose objection carries target, ground.rule, and scenario parts that are all present but empty strings
scenario.when: the record check validates the objection
